notes: 12448 noun entries; 33128 individually-decomposed inflected verb surface forms collapsed to 14378 verb ROOTS (grouped by root so every subject/tense inflection of the same verb sits together, same generalization principle as the adjective families below) -- pooled across 3 Swahili versions (SUV, NEN, BHN).

Adjective/associative/possessive/demonstrative forms are grouped by underlying concord family (e.g. mzuri/wazuri/kizuri/nzuri = one '-zuri' family) so the class system generalizes instead of looking like unrelated words.

Adjective families restricted to 9 curated consonant-initial reference-grammar stems (Ashton 1944; Mohammed 2001) -- vowel-initial stems (-eupe, -ekundu...) are excluded because their class-prefix contraction is irregular and was not guessed at.

Classes 11 and 15 have only a subject-marker entry in this project's tables (no adjective/associative/possessive/demonstrative concord table yet) -- agreement evidence (Page 2) could not be attempted for nouns of those classes; flagged, not silently skipped.

Kitaita translation candidate found for 2936/12448 nouns and 1285/14378 verb roots by the per-SURFACE-FORM method (Dice alignment on whole inflected words, best candidate across the 3 versions) -- a word with none listed has no alignment partner clean enough to clear Dice>=0.25 in any version, not a missing lookup.

NEW, separate ROOT-level re-alignment (2026-10-07, after the native speaker corrected the TAM table): strips subject+TAM from BOTH sides first (using the corrected Kitaita TAM table below) and aligns ROOTS instead of whole surface words, pooling every inflection into one count -- found for 4767/14378 roots, shown as 'root_level_kitaita_candidates'. This is the more reliable of the two: e.g. the 'kuw' (be) root was a weak, fragmented match per surface form (Dice 0.26-0.61 spread across a dozen distinct inflections) but root-level pooling finds a single clear signal (Kitaita 'kai', 228 shared verses, the dominant partner by a wide margin over the next-best 'ish' at 75) -- checked directly, not assumed.

Kitaita noun CLASS is a hypothesis copied from the aligned Swahili noun's class, not independently determined -- Kitaita has no known concord table. Where possible (2803/3522 candidates), this is cross-checked against an independent, weaker signal: whether the Kitaita noun co-occurs in the SAME verse with another word starting with this project's own CANDIDATE Kitaita subject-marker prefix for that class (induced from verb-paradigm contrast, Page 3) -- a genuine within-Kitaita agreement check, but a prefix-match, not a verified concord table or a verb detector; see each candidate's 'Kitaita-internal agreement check' field.

Each associative/possessive/demonstrative/adjective FORM above also carries its own best-aligned Kitaita candidate word (same Dice-alignment method as nouns/verbs) -- found for 6/6 associative forms and 22 adjective-family forms. 'za' (class 10) aligns to 'ra' (a plausible z/r sound correspondence). These are single-word alignments on short, very frequent function words, so treat a weak Dice score or a high competitor count here as considerably less reliable than the noun/verb cases.
